item.title: Solved: How to Properly Close IPython Notebook and Jupyter Sessions
item.description:
Solved: How to Properly Close IPython Notebook and Jupyter Sessions

When working with IPython notebooks and Jupyter servers, it’s important to understand the best ways to properly shut down your sessions to avoid resource wastage or leftover processes. Here are multiple solutions to ensure you close your Jupyter notebook cleanly, whether from the web interface, terminal, or through various system tools.

1. Closing from the Web Interface

The most straightforward way to close a notebook and halt its kernel is through the Jupyter Notebook web interface. From the File menu, select “Close and Halt”. This method is simple and will not only close the browser tab but will also ensure the kernel is properly stopped.

item.title: Top 10 Methods to Resolve the Jupyter Notebook '_xsrf' Argument Missing Error
item.description:
I’ve been facing a critical issue while working on a long-running script in Jupyter Notebook. Picture this: I have let the notebook process my data for over 26 hours. With a due deadline looming, the unexpected strikes—around the 21-hour mark, it inexplicably stopped saving my progress. The terminal chimed with a daunting message:

403 PUT /api/contents/[file.ipynb] (::1): '_xsrf' argument missing from POST

This is not just an error; it’s an urgent roadblock hindering my ability to save critical work. I’ve meticulously checked that I don’t have the LastPass extension installed or any ‘%’ characters in my code, yet the issue persists. What options do I have without restarting the entire notebook and rerunning my script?
